title: [YouPass Collect] - Students studying in six departments in an Australian university: 2009
prompt: The table below gives information about students studying in six departments in an Australian university in 2009. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table provides information about the percentages of female students, those whose first language is not English, and those born outside Australia across six departments at an Australian university in 2009.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, female students were predominant in English, Modern Languages, and History, while Physics, Math, and Chemistry attracted fewer women. Additionally, Modern Languages had the highest proportions of non-native English speakers and students born overseas, whereas History recorded the lowest figures in these two categories.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the arts-related departments, English had the highest proportion of female students, at 67%, followed by Modern Languages and History, at 63% and 58%, respectively. However, in terms of students whose first language was not English and those born overseas, Modern Languages stood out with figures of 41% and 54%, which were considerably higher than the corresponding percentages for English, at 16% and 27%, and History, at just 10% and 18%, making the latter the department with the smallest international student population.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the science departments, Chemistry had the lowest female representation, at only 29%, while Physics and Math recorded slightly higher figures of 37% and 42%, respectively. Regarding students with non-English first languages, the proportions ranged from 32% in Chemistry to 38% in Physics, with Math falling in between at 36%. Meanwhile, the percentages of students born outside Australia were relatively similar across these three departments, varying from 43% in Math to 47% in Chemistry, with Physics standing at 44%.
